parts.problem_md:
**Complete **each of the following sentences about web development layers.

The layer used to create the structure of a web page is called...
The layer that is a scripting language to control elements within a web page is called...

Anchors and hyperlinks are both used in HTML.

**Compare **an anchor with a hyperlink.

Your answer **must **include similarities and differences.
parts.solution_md:
The similarities and differences between anchors and hyperlinks include:

Any **four **of the following:

**Similarities **

- Both are links (in a web page) **[1 mark]**
- Both can be attached to icons/text/graphics **[1 mark]**
- Both are html tags used on web pages **[1 mark]**
- Both are used for navigation **[1 mark]**
- Both are coded as html tags starting with **[1 mark]**

**Differences **

- An anchor allows the user to move from one part of a web page to another part **[1 mark]**
- An anchor is a label that identifies a specific position in a document **OR **An anchor is within a hyperlink **[1 mark]**
- An anchor needs a point set in the document and a link **OR **A hyperlink only needs the link and a web address **[1 mark]**
- The code within an anchor will either be "name.." or "id.." **[1 mark]**
- An anchor determines a fixed point on a web page that is used as a bookmark **[1 mark]**
- An anchor can be placed at any point on a web page **[1 mark]**
- A hyperlink allows the user to move from one web page to another web page/website The code within a hyperlink can be "href..", "rel..”, “target..” **[1 mark]**
- A hyperlink can be attached to a block of text or image **[1 mark]**
- A hyperlink can be clicked on to cause another web page or part of the same web page to be displayed **[1 mark]**
- A hyperlink can redirect a user to an anchor by including its name **[1 mark]**
- A hyperlink is clickable **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> To gain full marks your response must have correct answers for **both** similarities and differences.

parts.problem_md:
The HTML of a web page consists of a head section and a body section.

**Explain **the purpose of the body section of HTML
parts.solution_md:
The purpose of the body section of HTML is:

Any **two **of the following:

- Defines the document’s body **[1 mark]**
- Contains all the elements of an HTML page **[1 mark]**
- Contains the content **[1 mark]**
- Contains style instructions **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
The HTML of a web page consists of a head section and a body section.

The head section can contain the link to the stylesheet.

**Identify **two other items found in the head section of HTML.
parts.solution_md:
Examples of other items found in the head section of HTML include:

Any **two **of the following:

- Document/page title **[1 mark]**
- Meta data **[1 mark]**
- Character set **[1 mark]**
- Styles Scripts **[1 mark]**
- Default target window/frame **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
Absolute and relative file paths are used in the content layer when creating a web page.

**Explain **the differences between an absolute file path and a relative file path.
parts.solution_md:
The difference between an absolute and relative file path is:

Any **two **of the following:

- Absolute file paths contain a complete URL/full file path with file name **[1 mark]**
- Contents of the URL include protocol, the website's domain name, specific file, subfolder, page name – 1 mark for at least two named **[1 mark]**
- Relative file paths only include a specific file or page **[1 mark]**
- This is relative to the current path **OR **starts from the same folder as the web page **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md: **Explain **why absolute file paths should **not **be used for hyperlinks to locally-saved web pages.
parts.solution_md:
Absolute file paths should not be used as:

Any **one **of the following:

- If the web pages have moved then the references refer to an old/previous file path **[1 mark]**
- Hyperlinks will not work **[1 mark]**
